set.tagline: Two fantasy armies, sixteen campaign missions, and heroes who insist on bringing their backpacks to war.
set.description: Loria is a free fantasy RTS with two races, two eight-mission campaigns, skirmishes and levelable heroes. Its DRM-free GOG edition runs on Windows, macOS and Linux; it is a single-player strategy game.

systemRequirements.min: Windows 7 SP1+ · SSE2-capable CPU · 4 GB RAM · DirectX 10 / shader model 4 graphics · 1.25 GB storage (GOG Windows minimum); Mac and Linux builds also available
systemRequirements.recommended: GOG does not publish a separate recommended tier for its Windows, Mac or Linux editions.

min.cpuText: CPU with SSE2 instruction support on Windows
min.gpuText: DirectX 10 / shader model 4-capable graphics on Windows
min.notes: Numbers and graphics API are GOG's Windows minimum. Mac and Linux downloads are offered, but equivalent per-OS numeric requirements are not published in this source.

recommended.notes: No distinct recommended hardware specification is published on the GOG page.

set.launcherInstall.note: Free DRM-free GOG release for Windows, macOS and Linux. Add it to your GOG library, then use the offline files for your OS or optional Galaxy client. PlayBound does not host a one-click archive for this game.

qualityBar.verdict: A familiar fantasy RTS with just enough hero busywork to make every skirmish feel personal.

set.longDescription:
Loria knows the kind of strategy game it wants to be. Peasants gather resources, buildings produce units, and two fantasy armies push toward each other across compact maps. The screen could have escaped from the era when a new RTS meant a fresh set of hotkeys to learn. Then a hero levels up, collects an item and asks for your attention in the middle of a base fight. That mixture of old-school economy and RPG detail is the game's central move.

There are two playable races and two campaigns of eight missions each. The missions give you a reason to learn the units and buildings before you take them into skirmish play. Six distinct heroes can level and carry items. Veteran units, upgrades and quest objectives add small decisions on top of the usual resource cycle. The result does not try to hide its inspirations. If you miss the period when fantasy RTS campaigns were full of earnest armies and elaborate bases, you will know what Loria is offering within a few minutes.

The important boundary is multiplayer. GOG currently labels Loria single-player, and its official feature list names campaigns and skirmish games without advertising a network mode. A skirmish here means playing against the game's AI, not joining a friend across the internet. We will not create a PlayBound party or dedicated-server claim from the word alone. Similarly, there is no verified native gamepad support or PlayBound Controls profile for a game designed around RTS mouse and keyboard input.

The GOG copy is free and DRM-free, and GOG supplies Windows, Mac and Linux versions. You may need to add it to a GOG library before downloading the offline installer for your OS; Galaxy is optional. The published Windows minimum is a CPU with SSE2, 4 GB RAM, DirectX 10-class graphics and 1.25 GB of free storage. Those figures should not be casually copied onto Mac and Linux as if every platform had the same graphics API. The old PlayBound Draft page gave Loria a 2026 release year and told players to bypass a Windows security warning for an open-source project. Both were errors: Loria released in 2018, and that warning was generic boilerplate unrelated to this GOG package.

Loria's appeal is direct. It gives you a complete pair of fantasy campaigns and the familiar pleasure of improving a base while a hero gets into trouble across the map. It may feel derivative to players who want a new form of strategy game; for someone who simply wants another campaign in this mold, it is worth a look, especially with no price attached.
set.whyWePickedIt: Loria offers two complete fantasy RTS campaigns and a free, DRM-free way to play them on three desktop platforms. Its hero items and veteran units add a little personal history to otherwise familiar base-building battles. We keep its limitations clear: skirmish is solo against AI, with no verified multiplayer or controller path.
set.thatOneThing: Your hero returns from a battle with a backpack full of loot while the workers behind him are still chopping the same trees.

installSteps.text: Add Loria to your GOG library for free, download its Windows offline installer or use optional GOG Galaxy, then install and launch the game.
Add Loria to your GOG library for free and download its Mac build from GOG. Follow the installation directions included with that package.
Add Loria to your GOG library for free and download its Linux build from GOG. Follow the installation directions included with that package.
Begin a campaign mission to learn resource gathering, buildings and hero inventory before choosing an AI skirmish.

firstPlaySteps.text: Use the opening campaign missions to learn each race's workers and buildings. Keep your hero near the army and inspect items after fights.

GOG lists Loria as single-player. Its skirmish games are against AI; no verified online, LAN or dedicated-server mode exists for this listing.
No official gamepad support or tested PlayBound Controls profile is documented. Use mouse and keyboard for RTS controls.
Two races, two eight-mission campaigns, six levelable heroes and AI skirmishes are listed by the developer.
